newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS - PRICES END FLAT TO UP SLIGHTLY.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS - PRICES END FLAT TO UP SLIGHTLY.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds ended flat to slightly higher Wednesday, while U.S. Treasuries managed to salvage more from a morning rally touched off by soft economic news.
Bonds' "volatility" prevented municipals from keeping pace with governments, a trader said.
"No one is sure which direction to take here," the trader said.

Market sources said both institutional bid lists and Street bid wanteds were circulating Wednesday, with longer-dated product accounting for much of what was offered. Lists totaled between $300 million and $400 million, they estimated.

Muni cash rose at least 3/8 of a point after morning data on July producer prices and retail sales, market sources said. A municipal analyst said dollar bonds opened up 3/8 of a point, were unchanged at noon, and ended flat to slightly higher.
The producer price index fell 0.1 percent both overall and in the core rate. Economists on average had expected a 0.1 percent gain in each.
Retail sales rose 0.6 percent overall versus forecasts for a 0.7 percent gain, and climbed 0.5 percent excluding autos, matching forecasts.

Thursday ushers in a fresh round of economic data, including the July Consumer Price Index. Economists polled by Reuters on average expect a 0.2 percent rise both overall and in the core rate, which excludes more volatile food and energy prices.

Also on deck are industrial production and capacity utilization figures for July. Economists expect a 0.2 percent increase in industrial production and an 83.5 percent reading for capacity utilization.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 19/32 at 96-24/32 to yield 6.63 percent in late New York trade. The bond had been up as much as 1-1/4 point early in the session.
In debt future, the September municipal contract was up 9/32 at 119-2/32. The September T-bond was up 12/32 at 112-27/32. The MOB spread was 199 ticks.
In new issues, Smith Barney Inc repriced $246 million Jacksonsville Electric Authority, Fla., bonds. The top yield at the repricing was 5.77 percent in 2037.
PaineWebber Inc restructured a $260 million Connecticut general obligation bond offering. While several maturities were added, he underwriter left the top yield unchanged at 5.40 percent in 2017.

Goldman Sachs & Co repriced and restructured New Jersey Health Care Facilities Financing Authority's $121 million bond deal for Atlantic Health System. While yields were adjusted in several maturities, Goldman left the top yield in 2027 unchanged at 5.50 percent.
Thursday's municipal bond sales are expected to total $213 million in 18 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Seven negotiated offerings totalled $105 million are scheduled, with a $35 million Jefferson Parish, La., offering through John Nuveen & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 11 sales totaling $108 million are scheduled. A $36 million Worcester, Mass., offering at 1100 EDT is the largest.
An additional five sales totaling $193 million remain on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the issues Thursday depending on market conditions.
